source.title: Interpreting CLIP: Insights on the Robustness to ImageNet Distribution Shifts
source.authors: Jonathan Crabb'e; P. Rodríguez; Vaishaal Shankar; L. Zappella; Arno Blaas

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses representation-space polysemanticity, but does not test neuron poles, neuron explanations, or any of the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports measurements of concepts encoded by last-layer right singular vectors (RSVs), not audits of neurons or neuron poles. These are recorded as related findings under versions ["none"]. Its results about outlier features, robustness, and concept counts are not neuron-pole interpretability results.
record.test_reason: The study probes last-layer representation-space directions (right singular vectors of the zero-shot head) of CLIP vision encoders with Broden concept probes to find robustness indicators. It does not audit neurons or neuron poles, test neuron explanations on held-out activations, score explanations by simulation, revisit InceptionV1's cat-and-car neuron, or build neuron attribution graphs. Its 'polysemanticity' count measures a different construct: concepts per SVD direction at AP ≥ 0.9. That count goes under fits_no_version. It mentions the cat/car neuron only as background (Appendix J).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The authors' main conclusions are that outlier features (high activation kurtosis) appear only in models robust to ImageNet shifts and so indicate robustness. Privileged directions are not an indicator, and the high number of unique concepts (and the resulting polysemanticity) tracks language supervision rather than robustness. The record's paraphrase underplays the outlier-feature result.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses activation kurtosis, SVD of classifier weights, and concept probing of representation-space directions; it does not use a neuron-pole audit or held-out neuron-explanation test.
record.method_sensitivity: The concept threshold is AP ≥ 0.9; the authors state the conclusions still hold at thresholds 0.8, 0.85, and 0.95.

fits_no_version.finding: Zero-shot CLIP vision encoders average 3 to 16 Broden concepts (AP ≥ 0.9) per last-layer right singular vector of the zero-shot head (Table 7). The authors call these models highly polysemantic.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Last-layer SVD directions of CLIP vision encoders are each linked to several Broden concepts under a probe-AP proxy. This is a direction-level, probe-based measure, not a neuron-pole audit.

fits_no_version.finding: CoCa zero-shot models encode 674 and 747 unique Broden concepts, falling to 530 and 629 after finetuning (Table 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The number of unique probe-detectable concepts in a representation space falls with ImageNet finetuning.

record.problems: The interpretability measurements concern last-layer representation-space directions and concept detection on Broden, not individual neuron poles or explanations tested on held-out activations. The reported polysemanticity is a proxy based on concept probes rather than manual feature visualization.
record.rows_left_out: No neuron-pole or held-out explanation results are reported. The paper also reports other representation analyses, including outlier-feature and robustness results, which do not measure the claim's neuron-pole interpretability subject.

untested.parts: Neuron-pole shares in other language models across scale and architecture
Reinterpretation of the InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron; mentioned only as background
Effect of architecture, regularization and tools on neuron interpretability
Whether explanations from activating examples predict held-out firing

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. The polysemanticity proxy counts concepts whose probe AP passes 0.9 along a direction. It does not show unrelated meanings per unit and does not involve neurons, so it cannot bear on V1–V7.

versions.untested_parts: Qwen3-32B neuron-pole shares and whether explanations tested on held-out activations identify one or two jobs.
Neuron-pole interpretability across language models, architectures, and scales.
Whether the InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron detects a shared pose or reflects recursive generalization rather than superposition.
Whether architecture, regularization, or tools explain messy neurons or change neuron interpretability estimates.
Attribution graphs built from a model's own neurons and whether they explain behavior without a trained replacement model.
Whether explanations fit to activating examples predict neuron firing on new examples.
Automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulated activations on new text.
